newsitem.title: USA: Rexene wants to increase revolving credit.
newsitem.headline: Rexene wants to increase revolving credit.

text.p: Rexene Corp said it is working with its bankers to increase a $150 million revolving credit facility to $225 million as a result of its tender offer for its shares.

Chief financial officer Geff Perera told a conference call after the company's first quarter earnings on Tuesday that $35 million of the revolving credit facility was earmarked for the tender for up to 11.5 percent of the company's outstanding shares.
Rexene, in the middle of a proxy fight with shareholders led by Wyser-Pratte, reiterated that it would accept a fully financed $16-per-share offer, but had received no formal offer.
A shareholder vote is scheduled for the end of April.
After announcing earnings per share of $0.32 for the first quarter of 1997 compared with $0.34 a year ago, the company's stock was down 1/8 at 13-5/8.
Chief executive Andy Smith told the conference call Rexene would see significant benefits from the startup of its olefins plant in Odessa, which is scheduled for completion in October 1998.
"We will enjoy an annual $25-$30 million cash benefit from the plant," he said.

The company also said that its REXflex polypropylene product line new capacity was producing at an annualised rate of 35 million pounds a year and that would rise to 75-80 million pounds and the company was exploring new applications.
"We are working with a major auto company on applications for interior components," Smith said.
